kicker: THE BACK OF THE BACK OF THE BOOK
title: The Trophy Case
dek: Real prizes, really awarded, for coming in last. History’s losers would like a word with the people who get these.
summary: Real prizes for finishing last, from the Tour de France’s lanterne rouge and the NFL’s Mr. Irrelevant to Eurovision’s nul points and the Razzies.

blocks.text: Turn the book upside down. Losers see the world from a different angle.
The answers printed upside down on this page belong to A Quiz That Doesn’t Like You (pp. 106–107), Crack the Losers’ Code (p. 109) and Find the Outsider (p. 108); they appear with those pieces.

items: Lanterne Rouge · Tour de France: The red lantern goes to the rider who finishes the Tour dead last, named for the light on the back of a train’s last car. You still have to ride every mile to get it.
The Lowsman · NFL Draft: The last pick in the draft is crowned “Mr. Irrelevant” and gets a trophy of a player fumbling the ball. Then a week of parties.
Nul Points · Eurovision: A song so unloved that no country gave it a single point. Fans keep a list, the way other people keep a list of champions.
The Razzie · Hollywood: Halle Berry showed up in 2005 to accept her Worst Actress award for Catwoman, holding her Oscar in the other hand.
The Sacko · Your fantasy league: Last place takes home a trophy and the shame that comes with it. Ours is a plunger in a goblet. See page 4.
The Wooden Spoon · Cambridge, 1800s–1909: For the worst math score that still passed: a wooden spoon lowered from the gallery on strings. The last one was an oar.
The Lottery Ball · NBA: Finish with the worst record and you get the best odds at next year’s top pick: 14%. Losing, rewarded in Ping-Pong balls.
The Booby Prize · Michigan card parties, 1880s: One unlucky loser went home with a live mouse in a box. Nobody recorded what the mouse thought.

sources: The Lanterne Rouge, Mr. Irrelevant, nul points, the Razzies (including Halle Berry’s 2005 acceptance) and the Sacko are widely reported.
